match.reason: None of the bank points teaches why people value texts for their ideas, style and social role; they cover text structure, the values shown within texts, context, text purposes and hybrid texts, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Why texts are valued
card: People value a text for different reasons. Three common ones are its ideas, its style and what it does in society.
Ideas
the text says something important about life, people or the world, such as courage, fairness or belonging. It makes readers think.
Style
the writer uses language well. Vivid images, a strong voice or a clever structure can make a text a pleasure to read or hear.
Role in society
the text does something for a community. A speech may help change a law, or a story may keep a culture's history alive by passing it on.
draft.remember: A text can be valued for its ideas, its style or its role in society.

a.q: Which reason for valuing a text is about its role in society?
opts: It was told for generations to keep a people's history alive
It uses vivid images that make a place feel real
It explores what it means to be brave
It has a clever twist in its final paragraph
a.why: A story that keeps a culture's history alive does a job for a community, so it is valued for its role in society. The vivid images and the twist are about style, and bravery is an idea.
a.clue: Which one is about what the text does for a group of people?

b.q: A speech given by Leila, a Year 8 student in Bathurst, is still played at her school each year. Listeners say the pictures she paints with her words make them feel as if they are there. Mainly, why is it valued?
opts: For its style, because of its strong use of language
For its ideas, because it explores a big theme
For its role in society, because it changed a law
For its role in society, because it is played each year
b.why: The listeners praise how Leila uses words to create pictures, which is style. Being played each year might tempt a student to pick role in society, but the scenario gives no sign that the speech does a job for a community.
b.clue: Look at what the listeners say they like about the speech.

a.best: It was told for generations to keep a people's history alive

b.best: For its style, because of its strong use of language

a.q: Which reason for valuing a text is about its role in society?
opts: It persuaded a town council to build a new library
It uses rhythm and rhyme that are fun to read aloud
It shows why forgiving a friend can be so hard
It tells its story backwards, from the end to the start
a.why: Persuading a council to build a library is something the text did for a community, so it is valued for its role in society. Rhythm, rhyme and telling a story backwards are about style, and forgiveness is an idea the text explores.
a.clue: Which one changed something in the real world for a group of people?
